what_this_is: The rule inventory of the CIC_L specification against pinned Lean 4's kernel sources (self-proof plan unit S7; the proven-core plan's KR2 inventory). Every function, case arm and hardcoded-constant use of the pinned files is claimed by a row; every rule row names the CIC_L items that state it and says specified, partial or unspecified. scripts/check_cic_l_rule_inventory.py re-derives both sides and prints the counts; no count is written here.

how_to_read.status: specified: the theory has an item that states this rule family, named in cic_l. partial: it states part, and `missing` names the rest. unspecified: no item states it; `groundwork` may name data the theory already has for it. A status is the recorded reading of whoever wrote the row. The gate checks that each named item exists with that kind in that file, and never that it is adequate.
how_to_read.kind: rule: deleting the code would change which judgments the kernel accepts as instances of a rule. strategy: the code only orders the rules it names in uses_rules. infrastructure: object plumbing, caches, printing.
how_to_read.extension: A family that hardcodes Lean constants beyond the core calculus. plan_requires_derived_rule says whether the self-proof plan requires it as a derived rule (unit S6 for Nat and String literals).
how_to_read.anchors: file is relative to upstream.root; lines are 1-based and inclusive; sha256 is of those raw lines. A whole-function anchor has the function's span; a function split between rows has every code line and case arm claimed by some part.
how_to_read.control: Plan unit E6 / M3. Each constructor item of a rule carrier names its negative control: {theorem, file}, a ground theorem `<constructor>_control` stating `Refutes .<constructor> ...` (with that premise deleted the judgment derives a statement it refutes as written), or {none: reason} where no single deleted premise lets the judgment derive a statement it can be shown to refute (zero constructors of CICL.CoreJudgmentIn remain none). The gate checks the name and the statement across spec.control_roots; crates/clean-olean/tests/cic_l_level.rs and crates/clean-olean/tests/cic_l_model.rs check the admitted theorems and what Refutes, Closed and Mutation mean.

grouping_rule: One row per rule family, where a family is the unit of specification work: one typing rule per term former, one row per reduction, one per definitional-equality rule, one per stage of inductive admission, one per generated artifact. A dispatch function is split by line range so each arm goes to its family. Where the kernel dispatches on hardcoded constants, constants that share one implementation function share a row, and the row names each of them.
out_of_scope: KR2 names four files; inductive.h and quot.h are pinned with them because iota, K, structure eta of a major premise and quotient reduction are defined there. Everything else under src/kernel is outside this inventory, in particular environment.cpp (admission of axioms, definitions, theorems, opaque and mutual definitions), expr.cpp (lit_type), instantiate.cpp, abstract.cpp, local_ctx.cpp, declaration.cpp, equiv_manager.cpp and type_checker.h. A rule those files state is not counted here.

rows.title: A sort has the next sort as its type
A constant has its declared type at the given universe arguments
rows.note: The safety check and the declared-universe check that sit inside infer_constant are the rows constant-safety and universe-params-declared.

rows.title: Every universe parameter a checked declaration mentions is one it declares
rows.note: The kernel enforces this while inferring a declaration's type and value (m_lparams). The specification states it where a declaration is admitted, as LevelScoped of the whole type and value (ConstantAdmission.typeScoped and valueValid, FamilyHeaderView.universeScoped, ConstructorCertificate.universeScoped), not as a premise of the sort and constant rules. Plan units S0 and S1 restate it as a premise.

rows.title: A safe declaration uses no unsafe or partial constant
rows.note: Declarations under definition_safety::unsafe or as partial definitions are permanently outside the proved CIC_L theory (docs/DECISIONS.md, 2026-11-15): WfSignature admits exclusively ConstantDecl.Safe constants (wfSignature_constant_safe) and refuses every unsafe or partial payload variant.

rows.title: A local variable has the type its context gives it
rows.note: CoreJudgmentIn.bvar states de Bruijn context typing, and CICL.LocalContextRules.inferFVar_iff_lookupType proves exact locally-nameless correspondence with type_checker::infer_fvar via openWithFVars/closeFVars (with choice-free semantic soundness in CICLModel/LocalContextSemantics.lean).

rows.title: Quot.lift and Quot.ind applied to Quot.mk reduce
rows.missing: General quotient packets satisfying the pinned Eq-shape guard remain outside this slice. The actual typed equations here require the exact literal Eq/Eq.refl and four-primitive packet; quotient primitive admission and checker acceptance remain separate outstanding work.
rows.note: The lift constructor preserves both sort bounds, exact primitive citations and all six literal argument typings, including a : alpha. Both endpoints are derived from these guards. The induction equation is Prop-only, with actual typed endpoints and proposition classification, and is derived by the existing proof-irrelevance rule. This is a logical specification, not an executable quotient normalizer or admission rule.

Universe-level equivalence
rows.note: The specification states the relation by evaluation (SemEq), sortCong consumes it, and CICL.Level.eqv_iff_semEq proves that CICL.Level.eqv is both sound and complete for SemEq. Lean 4's C++ level normalizer + is_geq_core is strictly incomplete for SemEq on nested imax (CICL.Level.imaxSeparation_cpp_incomplete).

rows.title: Universe-level order
rows.note: The specification states the relation by evaluation (SemLE), consumed by the constructor universe bound, and CICL.Level.leq_iff_semLE proves that CICL.Level.leq is both sound and complete for SemLE. CICL.Level.cppIsGeqCore models level.cpp's is_geq_core and CICL.Level.imaxSeparation_cpp_incomplete witnesses its imax incompleteness relative to SemLE.

Whether a recursor eliminates into every universe or into Prop only

A nested occurrence is replaced by an auxiliary family of the same mutual block
The constants of the auxiliary block are translated back to the nested form
The weak-head-normal-form loop
rows.reason: Chooses which reduction is tried next, returns terms that are already values, reduces the head of an application before its redex, and caches results. Each step it takes is a step of one of the rule rows it names.

rows.title: The order in which definitional-equality rules are tried
rows.reason: Sequences the easy cases, weak-head normalization of both sides, and the rule rows it names; answers false when none applies. It adds no equation of its own.

rows.title: Lazy delta reduction
rows.reason: Decides which side of an equation is unfolded first, by reducibility hint, and tries argument-wise comparison of two applications of the same definition before unfolding. Every unfolding is a step of reduce-delta; the argument-wise comparison is application congruence over defeq-constant-levels.

rows.title: The Bool.true shortcut and the eagerReduce mode
rows.reason: An argument of the form `eagerReduce _ _` switches a mode in which Nat reduction is tried on open terms and a term compared with Bool.true is fully reduced first; the same shortcut applies to any closed term. Both only choose when whnf is called: the equations they find are whnf steps of the rule rows named here. The names eagerReduce and Bool.true are hardcoded, and nothing here gives either constant a rule.

rows.title: Type inference: dispatch, cache, refusals
rows.reason: Dispatch on the term former, the result cache, the interrupt check, and the two refusals that delimit the input: a loose bound variable and a metavariable (the specification's Expr has no metavariable former).

rows.title: The type checker's C++ objects, caches and globals
rows.reason: Constructors and destructor of the checker and its state, the failure cache, and the tables of hardcoded constants built at start-up. The constants themselves are claimed where they are used.

rows.title: Functions the pinned files define and never call
rows.reason: Each is exported for callers outside the kernel's checking path (the elaborator, the runtime) and is called by no function in the pinned files: eta_expand builds an eta-expanded term; the is_stuck pair reports why a recursor application did not reduce (the source says it affects the elaborator's effectiveness, not the kernel's correctness); quot_is_decl names the quotient constants.

rows.title: Lookups of a constant's kind
rows.reason: Read what kind of constant a name is in the environment; they state no rule.

rows.title: The inductive module's C++ objects and globals
rows.reason: Constructors of the helper classes, one-line wrappers around the type checker and the local context, and the start-up tables. The name-generator prefixes are not Lean constants.

rows.title: The quotient module's globals
rows.reason: Build and free the table of the four quotient names.

rows.title: The level datatype: constructors, accessors, printing
rows.reason: Raw constructors and runtime accessors of the level object, its hash and packed header, a structural total order for containers (is_lt, called by no function in the pinned files), traversal, printing, the exported C entry points and the start-up table. The grammar of levels is CICL.Level; level metavariables have no counterpart there and the kernel refuses them in declarations.
